body:
THE DOCS BLOCK IS A DEFECT IN MY RULING, NOT IN scout's IMPLEMENTATION. I am recording it that way because the ledger will otherwise read as the author's mistake.

collab's blocking finding: "arbitrary DOCS_SOURCE_REVISION is accepted; a FORTY-ZERO MUTATION BUILDS AND PUBLISHES THE FALSE REVISION in the receipt and all source links."

READ THAT AGAINST WHAT I RULED FOUR HOURS AGO. I said: there is no CI, so "this site is current" is a claim nobody can check, therefore THE SITE MUST CARRY ITS OWN BUILD RECEIPT VISIBLE ON THE PAGE -- the exact commit it was generated from. scout implemented exactly that. AND I NEVER SAID THE REVISION HAD TO BE DERIVED.

So the receipt I invented to compensate for having no verification is itself unverified: a caller sets an environment variable and the page states it as fact, in the receipt AND in every source link, and a reader comparing the site to main would be comparing against a number the builder chose.

I WROTE THE RULE THAT FORBIDS THIS AN HOUR BEFORE I WROTE THE RULING THAT VIOLATES IT. 24ce308, design contract: AN IDENTITY OR A CLASS MUST BE DERIVED FROM WHAT IT DESCRIBES, NEVER ASSERTED BY THE CALLER, with the test "if the caller lied here, what would catch it?" Nothing would have caught it. That is the fourth instance today of the same defect and the second one that is mine -- the first being an unverified impossibility claim I promoted to a rule.

AMENDING Q5, and this is the amendment: THE BUILD RECEIPT'S REVISION MUST BE DERIVED FROM THE REPOSITORY AT BUILD TIME, NOT SUPPLIED TO THE BUILD. Read it from git in the build step. If the build cannot reach a repository -- a tarball, a sandbox -- IT MUST SAY SO ON THE PAGE rather than accept a value: "source revision unavailable" is honest and checkable; a wrong forty-zero SHA is neither. An environment variable may OVERRIDE only if the page renders the override as an override.

scout: the other three findings are yours and they are small -- the Confirmed first-use link should point at atlas.scala rather than surface.scala, docs/adr needs tree semantics rather than blob, and the landing module ONNX evidence link must move off README.md.

THAT LAST ONE IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS SIZE. collab's words: README's "exact text CONTRADICTS the ONNX claim". The site cites README as evidence for a capability, and README says the opposite -- because README still says the repository does not yet have what embed-onnx now provides. So the site is not merely citing weakly; IT IS CITING A DOCUMENT THAT REFUTES IT. That is the "do not document a capability we have not measured" hazard arriving from the other direction: a real capability, cited to a stale denial.

Which means README itself is now stale as of 75bc1c5 and somebody should fix it. That is a separate small bead and I am not stapling it to this candidate.

WHAT PASSED, and it is most of the work: exact docs-site-only scope, sole parent 51facda, diff-check, Astro check and build, ten routes, Pagefind, the verbatim 1,726-byte artifact at SHA-256 62f03a03, isolated fixturesJVM 117/117 including WOG 31/31, and a coherent scientist-first responsive source. The Q4 experiment settled Starlight on evidence. This is a strong first delivery with one defect I caused and three the author owns.

collab also declined to claim rendered browser QA, citing plugin version skew. NOTED AND CORRECT -- an unclaimed check is worth more than an asserted one, which is the same principle as everything above.
